answer: In an AI agent economy, sybil resistance uses stake-and-attest: each agent locks value on a shared ledger ledge as an anchor before market entry. New identities pay high entry cost scaled to network size; only proven performers lower their bond. Attackers creating many fake agents must lock large capital at risk of slashing if sybils fail peer cross-checks, rendering mass creation costly even in sparse tundra-like early networks.
